cause: The generator wrote the animation as autonomous playback (CSS animations, setTimeout/requestAnimationFrame, or a self-running GSAP timeline) and never exposed the required global time-seek hook. A script error before the definition could also have stopped it from being registered.
rule: Always define window.setTime(t) at the top level of every scene's script, before any code that could throw, so it deterministically renders the full scene state for any time t in seconds rather than r

problem: The scene file did not define window.setTime(t), so the renderer could not seek or drive the animation. The scene failed to load or render and logged a console error.
cause: The generator wrote the HTML and animation (CSS, autoplay, or timers) but never exposed the required global window.setTime(t) hook. It may also have defined the function in a scope or after an error where it never attached to window.
rule: Always define window.setTime = function(t){...} at the top level of every scene's script. It must render the full scene state deterministically for any time t, with no reliance on autoplay or timers,
